output.summary: Approve independently reviewed G1043 revision2: reuse canonical ID sharding for local verification, preserve test assertions, measure integer test cost for reviews/merge approvals, opt-in parallel command lanes within shared CPU budget, and bounded informational target-history baseline lookup. All3 review findings resolved; source audit established obsolete property isolation can be removed without weaker assertions. Product changes are distinct from installed-policy adoption; the separate policy PR remains for explicit requested owner approval.

responses.design:reopen:1: fixed: add verification_plan_sha256 excluding goal-specific commands; select newest eligible merged source once and independently qualify baseline.verification against repository hash/environment. Whole-run mismatch remains unavailable while matching repository delta/status/provenance/caveat is shown. No second scan/older fallback/new state; acceptance/tests/docs cover both scopes and missing/budget-exhausted evidence.

output.summary: Revision 3 fixes the cross-goal comparison gap with a separate repository-plan hash and independently qualified nested verification comparison against the same newest eligible merged source. A changed targeted command leaves total-time comparison unavailable while preserving a matching canonical verification delta, with its own provenance and explicit concurrency/load caveat. No extra lookup, older-source fallback or new state is added; prior CPU, isolation-audit and bounded-lookup corrections remain unchanged.

findings.text: Section 3 does not preserve an inherited total CPU budget: it splits observed C first and then independently clamps each lane by ZZZOPS_TEST_WORKERS. With C=20 and a parent budget of 4 this allocates 4+4=8 workers; with parent=1 it still launches two one-worker lanes despite the single-CPU fallback. Compute the effective total C=min(available CPUs, validated parent budget) before deciding parallel versus sequential execution and before splitting it, then pass lane allocations whose simultaneous sum never exceeds that effective C. Add parent-budget-smaller-than-half-C and parent=1 cases to the arithmetic/overlap tests; distinguish observed CPUs from the effective allocation in recorded metadata.

Sections 1 and 3 retain exclusive test scheduling but define exclusivity only inside each local runner pool. With two parallel command lanes, runner A can finish its concurrent pool and start LINUX_EXCLUSIVE_TESTS while runner B (or an ordinary targeted command) is still running. CPU budgets do not prevent this overlap. The current runner explicitly keeps test_engine_property.NoDeadEndPropertyTests.test_random_portfolios outside its pool; the new design promises to preserve that exclusivity. Specify the boundary and a compatible execution rule: coordinate retained exclusive phases across the simultaneously launched lanes, or use a conservative sequential arrangement when such coordination cannot be guaranteed. Do not claim job-wide isolation from a per-invocation join. Add a barrier-based two-lane test where one lane reaches its exclusive phase while the other still has active work, and prove the chosen rule.

The informational baseline lookup in section 5 has no bounded completion contract, and section 4 explicitly ends the shared command timeout and measured wall interval before that lookup starts. Normal read_state skips closed goal bodies; the proposal adds reads of those bodies plus target first-parent traversal/ancestry/code-tree checks. Catching missing objects/exceptions and avoiding network calls does not bound work as the closed portfolio and target history grow, so a successful verification can remain in run_tests arbitrarily long for an optional delta. Specify a small bounded local-work/deadline policy covering candidate documents and target-history/tree work, and return an explicit unavailable reason if it is exhausted. Reuse existing snapshot/evidence and clocks; no timing database or new persistent index is necessary. Test a large/capped candidate stream and history traversal to prove completion, no fallback to a convenient older candidate, and unchanged verification success when lookup is incomplete.

output.summary: Revision 2 resolves all three findings: one parent-capped CPU budget precedes lane allocation; source-audited removal of the stale exclusive property entry preserves every semantic assertion; bounded read-only baseline lookup returns unavailable on incomplete evidence rather than an older partial match. No new finding or owner-only question.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Owner, verbatim: "Yeah I think we should do sharded test runs, but we also need to be keeping an eye on test run times. Does the test review lens check test run times for sanity?"

Facts (2026-11-02, G1025 branch, 20-core machine):
- run_tests runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s .agents` on one core: about 20 to 25 minutes, up from 11 to 14 minutes earlier the same day; one run hit a 25-minute limit. Machine load stayed under 3.
- The same suite split by file, 12 files at a time, took 491 s, bounded by the two slowest files: test_engine_lenses.py 487 s (62 tests) and test_engine_branching.py 474 s (56 tests). Next: test_engine_github 200 s, test_engine_review_lenses 169 s, test_engine_owner_questions 155 s.
- CI already shards with .github/scripts/run_product_validation.py; locally its discovery failed only because a G1025 test module collected TestCases twice (fixed on G1025).
- Neither the review_tests prompt nor the Tests lens mentions run time, and run_tests' recorded per-command `seconds` are never shown to a reviewer or the owner.
- G1025's run_tests (2026-11-02) took 2,686 s: its recorded test_design command (test_engine_branching.py, 497 s) and then the full suite (2,189 s, single core), which runs that same file again. Owner, verbatim: "This run is 40m and counting...". When verification already runs the full suite, run_tests should not run the targeted commands separately (or should run them in parallel).

Scope:
- One repository command that runs the canonical suite sharded in parallel on the local machine (reusing run_product_validation.py's inventory and balancing, worker count from the CPU count), with a single pass/fail and per-shard timings; this repository's verification.commands use it through a policy PR the owner approves.
- Split or speed up the slowest test files so no single file dominates (target: a full local run under 5 minutes on an 8+ core machine), without weakening what they assert.
- Test cost becomes a reviewed quantity: review_tests and the Tests lens ask for the run time of new or changed tests (from the run, not a guess) and flag disproportionate cost (sleeps, repeated full journeys where a unit check would do, wall-clock bounds); run_tests records per-command and total seconds and the delta against the last run on the integration branch, and approve_merge shows it.
- Keep the engine small: durations are already recorded by checks.run; prefer showing them over new machinery.

Acceptance:
- A full local run of this repository's suite completes in under 5 minutes on the owner's machine and still runs every test once (discovery has no duplicate ids).
- A review_tests card for a goal that adds a slow test shows its measured cost, and the prompt asks the reviewer to judge it.
- The approve_merge item shows run_tests total time and its change versus trunk.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: Run local verification sharded, and make test run time a reviewed quantity
